answer: A stake-and-attestation market resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable bond and earn peer endorsements before gaining weight. Faking many identities is costly because every copy must pay the bond and do verifiable work, while an honest agent's record grows like an opal formed layer by layer and cannot be copied to a new identity. Like an atlas mapping only verified routes, the registry lists just attested agents; a harbor-style quarantine holds newcomers at low trust until their work checks out, so weak copies yield less influence than one honest, bonded identity.
